verdict.summary: Analysing has a materially mature Symfony 8.1/PHP 8.4 implementation, strong repository quality tooling, browser-level behavioral coverage infrastructure, and active RC hardening, but it is not yet release-candidate complete because the current commit is untagged and the working tree contains staged or unstaged destructive changes affecting gating configuration and a domain-hygiene guard.
strengths: Symfony 8.1 and PHP 8.4 baseline with Doctrine ORM/DBAL and explicit component dependencies.
Repository includes PHPStan at maximum level, PHPUnit, PHP CS Fixer, Psalm, PHPMD, Qodana, Gitleaks, gating, coverage, schema-parity, and standalone smoke commands.
Playwright-based browser tests and a behavioral-coverage command provide explicit UI-level QA infrastructure.
Recent commits show focused canonical migration and RC verification hardening.
Docker, Docker Compose, CI workflows, QA environment checks, migrations, and runtime smoke checks provide substantial operational readiness.
risks: Current commit has no exact release tag.
Working tree is not clean: the Analysing gating profile and analytics-domain-hygiene guard are deleted while composer.json is modified.
Composer production dependencies use multiple dev-master component versions, increasing reproducibility and release-governance risk.
Repository identity still exposes historical Analytics naming in package metadata, IDE metadata, scripts, and documentation, which may indicate residual canonical migration debt.
Antora component navigation/index files are not present in the repository facts, so documentation integration is not fully evidenced.
next_actions: Resolve and verify the current working-tree deletions and composer.json modification before RC acceptance.
Run the repository gate, PHPUnit suite, PHPStan max analysis, schema parity, standalone smoke, and Playwright behavioral tests on a clean candidate commit.
Tag the verified RC commit once all required gates are green.
Finish remaining Analysing-versus-Analytics naming reconciliation where legacy names are no longer intentional.
Review dev-master inter-component dependencies and establish a reproducible release dependency policy.
notes: Assessment is based exclusively on the deterministic facts embedded in the authoritative prompt.
The repository is currently on rc/analysing-canon-vendor-20260913 at commit 9ea6128f0ac2bbd5c59e7cd3f973b2a2144d65c1.

product.summary: Component identity is materially established as Analysing, with a dedicated package, repository, runtime surface, documentation, and RC branch, although residual Analytics naming remains visible in repository metadata and tooling.
risks: Legacy Analytics naming may blur the final canonical component identity.
improvements: Complete intentional naming reconciliation and document any retained Analytics terminology.

architecture.summary: Architecture maturity is strong: the repository is Symfony 8.1 oriented, uses explicit component dependencies, Doctrine persistence, canonical gating, migrations, and recent commits dedicated to canonical migration and RC hardening.
risks: Multiple dev-master component dependencies reduce architectural release reproducibility.
Deletion of the component gating profile and domain-hygiene guard in the current working tree could weaken canonical enforcement if intentional changes are not replaced equivalently.
improvements: Restore or intentionally replace canonical guard coverage, then verify the clean candidate through the component gate.
Adopt a reproducible dependency-release policy for inter-component packages.

runtime.summary: Runtime readiness is materially present through Symfony console/application bootstrap, Doctrine schema validation, standalone smoke checks, Docker assets, and explicit PHP 8.4/Symfony 8.1 requirements.
risks: Runtime validation results are not included in the supplied facts, so successful execution of smoke and schema commands is not proven for the current commit.
Current working-tree changes may alter the exact candidate being assessed.
improvements: Execute standalone smoke and schema-parity commands on the clean RC candidate and retain their results in the assessment pipeline.

qa.summary: QA depth is strong for a pre-RC component, with PHPUnit, coverage generation, PHPStan max analysis, PHP CS Fixer, Psalm, PHPMD, Qodana, QA environment checks, Playwright browser tests, and behavioral UI coverage tooling.
risks: The supplied facts prove tooling presence but not green results for the current commit.
Deletion of a hygiene guard from the working tree may reduce static quality enforcement if not replaced.
improvements: Run and capture green results for PHPUnit, coverage, PHPStan max, repository gating, and Playwright behavioral coverage on the exact clean RC commit.

ops.summary: Operational and governance posture is strong, with GitHub workflows, Docker packaging, Gitleaks configuration, repository gating, QA environment validation, migration checks, and recent RC verification hardening.
risks: The assessed commit is not exactly tagged.
The dirty working tree prevents treating the present filesystem state as an immutable release candidate.
improvements: Clean and verify the working tree, execute the full operational gate set, and create an exact tag for the accepted candidate.

market.summary: Business-facing alignment remains materially present through a clearly named Analysing component and integration with the wider Smartresponsor component ecosystem, but the supplied evidence is primarily engineering-focused rather than market-validation focused.
risks: No new market or user-adoption evidence is included in the deterministic facts.
Residual Analytics naming may reduce portfolio-facing clarity.
improvements: Preserve the existing market assessment while adding explicit owner-facing purpose and ecosystem-role documentation during a future scheduled assessment.

overall.summary: Analysing is a strong pre-RC component with mature architecture, QA, and operational controls; the principal remaining RC blockers evidenced here are an unclean working tree, deleted canonical guard assets, dev-master dependency reproducibility, and absence of an exact release tag.
risks: Current filesystem state is not an immutable release candidate.
Required quality tooling is present, but green execution results for this exact candidate are not included in the facts.
Inter-component dev-master dependencies and residual naming debt remain release-quality concerns.
improvements: Produce a clean candidate, resolve guard/profile deletions, run all defined quality and runtime gates, then tag the verified commit.
